articles.title: Patrick Mahomes teams up with eyewear giant Oakley as $213 signature collection adds a stylish twist to his highly anticipated NFL comeback
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is getting ready for his return to the NFL, and his latest move has added a stylish touch to the comeback story. The Kansas City Chief.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is getting ready for his return to the NFL, and his latest move has added a stylish touch to the comeback story. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has unveiled a new signature eyewear collection with Oakley, giving fans a closer look at the partnership just days before his expected return. With his knee recovery nearing its biggest test, Mahomes now has another reason to keep the spotlight firmly on him.Patrick Mahomes Oakley collection brings Chiefs style to new releaseThe new Patrick Mahomes Signature Series arrives at an interesting moment in the quarterback’s career. Oakley, which began working with Mahomes in 2024, has built the latest collection around details that connect directly with the Chiefs star.The range includes three standout styles. The Permian features a Black Ink frame, matte clear pad-print stems and an anodized red icon. Its Prizm Ruby lenses are designed to improve contrast and color, making the pair suitable for everyday outdoor use.Mahomes’ other two choices, the Sutro Lite Sweep and Resistor Sweep, take a darker approach. They feature Dark Galaxy frames, Trans Black Ink stems and Prizm Black lenses. Chiefs red and polished gold details add the team-inspired finish without making the glasses feel like simple fan merchandise.Comfort also gets attention. All three designs include black nose pads and ear socks. The packaging follows the same premium theme, with a matte black sleeve, gold Oakley foil and a custom microfiber bag carrying both Oakley and Mahomes branding.The collection is already available online, with prices starting at around $213.The timing makes the launch even more notable. Oakley introduced the series alongside the 2026 NFL Kickoff period, putting Mahomes’ name in front of football fans just as the new season begins.Patrick Mahomes comeback adds bigger meaning to Oakley launchThe eyewear release comes while Mahomes remains at the center of one of the NFL’s biggest Week 1 storylines.The three-time Super Bowl champion has spent the offseason working his way back from torn ACL and LCL ligaments in his left knee. The injury required surgery in December and kept him away from preseason action.Now, the quarterback is much closer to playing again.Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Tuesday that there is a strong chance Mahomes will start against the Denver Broncos in Week 1. Reid has not made the decision official, however, meaning Mahomes still has to avoid any late setback before Monday night.That uncertainty has not stopped the quarterback from pushing through his rehabilitation. After receiving clearance for full football activities in late July, Mahomes became a regular participant in Chiefs practices.His return will also come against a Denver team that has won Kansas City’s last two regular-season meetings. That gives the matchup an added edge, particularly with Mahomes attempting to make his first meaningful appearance since the injury.For now, the new Oakley collection offers a lighter side to an otherwise serious comeback. The real test, though, will arrive when Mahomes puts on his helmet rather than his sunglasses and takes the field again.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 49ers vs. Rams betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props for the Australia game
articles.summary: Our NFL handicappers break down their favorite bets on the game and player props for 49ers-Rams in Australia.
articles.body:
After some backlash to playing a Week 1 game on a Friday — a gray area with regards to legal agreements that the pro league wouldn't step on a night reserved for amateur football in America — the NFL has moved the Super Bowl champion Seahawks' opener up a night, while still sending two teams abroad for Thursday night.

In what feels like a punishment for not beating the Seahawks to at least get to the Super Bowl, and in lieu of driving on Interstate 5, the Rams and 49ers have been sent to Melbourne, Australia to open their season with a key divisional matchup.

Yahoo Sports betting writers Matt Russell and Jeremy Pond give their best bets for the matchup.

San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (-3.5, 48.5) in Melbourne, Australia

Russell: Across the 16-game Week 1 odds board, there hasn't been a ton of line movement since the schedule was announced amid the annual, mid-May social-media frenzy, but what our game handicap pre-supposes that there should have been here?

The Rams opened -3 (+100) for this neutral-site tilt — an obvious implication that the Rams were considered, yes, about 3 points better than the 49ers. Of course, since that line became available, L.A. put together something of its own parlay, making a trade that didn't just bring the Rams Myles Garrett , but brought Aaron Donald out of retirement (restarting the clock on his inevitable first-ballot Hall-of-Fame induction).

Beyond the obvious, Garrett's grading out as the best pass rusher in the sport by PFF, with Garrett on the field, the Browns consistently ranked near the top of the NFL in pass-rush win rate, largely because Garrett commanded a league-high double-team rate of roughly 30%. Ipso facto, we can expect a similar impact with him joining the Rams, even with Donald skipping the opener .

Is that worth just a half-point, even off of a key number?

Let's take a look at last season's betting market, and the matchups for the 49ers-Rams games.

The Niners stunned the Rams in overtime in L.A., in a Week 5 game started by Mac Jones , which was lined at -8.5, or around -7 on a neutral field. Later in the season, again with Jones starting in Santa Clara in Week 10, the Rams closed as 6-point favorites on the road, or around -7 on a neutral field.

A season later, maybe Brock Purdy is a 4-point upgrade on his backup, but Jones was 33-of-39, for 319 passing yards in a 42-26 home loss last season (and was turnover-free for 342 yards in the first meeting), so how much more can Purdy improve upon that?

That's not the only roster upgrade for the 49ers, though, as they'll have Fred Warner and Nick Bosa back as well. Of course, the Rams match that with Garrett and the earlier additions of Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson from Kansas City , addressing the issues they had at cornerback last season.

In the end, the 49ers are dining out on a 12-5 record in 2025, but after a Week 1 win in Seattle , outside of the quasi-miracle win in L.A., and stealing a victory in Philadelphia in the divisional round, San Francisco was outplayed by the best teams on last year's schedule ( Houston , Jacksonville , Tampa Bay ), and demonstrably in rematches with the Seahawks and Rams.

Finally, it's been reported that head coach Sean McVay and the Rams have done extensive studies on how to handle the travel in international games, and their "turn-and-burn" strategy worked well in a 35-7 win over Jacksonville — England regulars — last season.

Even though we're not capturing a key number in a game that could easily be lined a couple points higher, look for the Rams to send something of a message to the rest of the league against a familiar foe.

RB Christian McCaffrey under 60.5 rushing yards (-110, Bet365)

Russell: Age is just a number, but McCaffrey's is now 30.

The 2025 Comeback Player of the Year ran into literal trouble when facing the Rams last season, long before they added Garrett for this game. McCaffrey tried the Rams' defense 34 times on the ground, totaling 87 yards in the two games, for an average of 2.55 yards per carry.

While that was his toughest matchup, McCaffrey and the Niners' offensive line struggled to find space. Of the 17 players to run for at least 1,000 yards, McCaffrey was the only one to average less than 4.0 YPC.

He'll be a weapon in the passing game, as always, but likely needing more than 15 carries, and maybe as many as 20, in a game that could get away from the Niners, we'll take the under on another future Hall of Famer.

RB Blake Corum over 43.5 rushing yards (-110, Bet365)

Russell: Corum's usage went from "in case of emergency" in his 2024 rookie season as Kyren Williams ' backup, to "we need to get this guy more touches" in Year 2.

Per our look at 32 bets for 32 teams article last week, Corum's share of carries went up to 36% last season, on the strength of a 41.5% rate in the final 11 games.

Corum ran for 5.1 yards per carry, so the hope is that all he needs Thursday is around eight carries — a number Corum got in eight of the final 11 regular-season games, and two of three in the playoffs.

You'd think trekking across the Pacific Ocean would accentuate the desire to split the work in the opener, against an opponent that was second-to-last in the NFL in defensive success rate against opponents' rushing plays.

TE Terrance Ferguson longest reception over 15.5 yards (-115, Bet365)

Russell: As a rookie, Ferguson was a designated hitter — a talented receiver in a big body that the Rams would spring on opponents, seemingly out of nowhere, and deep down the field. Eight of his 11 regular-season receptions were for at least 18 yards.

Ferguson is listed as questionable for Thursday night, so if he's unable to go, this bet will be refunded.

RB Christian McCaffrey over 4.5 receptions (-106 at FanDuel)

Pond: The 30-year-old running back is coming off a campaign where he recorded 113 catches on 142 targets for a San Francisco side that finished 12-5 in regular season before a 41-6 blowout loss to Seattle ended its Super Bowl dreams.

That said, I fully expect McCaffrey to pick up where he left off last season. He will remain the No. 1 safety valve for Brock Purdy for dump-offs and screen passes due to the fact the 49ers quarterback is going to feel the heat all night from Myles Garrett and the Rams defense.

And when you throw in the fact the San Francisco wide-receiving corps is anything but healthy, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic McCaffrey can get the job done.

Overall, McCaffrey cleared this number in four of San Francisco's last five games – including the playoffs – last season. He also caught eight passes in each game against Los Angeles. McCaffrey wound up with at least five receptions in 15 of 19 contests, so I'm confident he will cash this prop bet and have a big night for the underdog 49ers.

Kyren Williams over 1.5 receptions (-148 at FD) and 15+ receiving yards (+140 at FD)

Pond: When it comes to finishing games with at least two receptions, Williams was a model of consistency for the Rams a season ago. He had at least two catches in his final six games of the regular season and postseason. As for his full-season numbers, he wound up with two or more receptions on 14 occasions in 20 games for a 70% hit rate.

I know everyone is aware of the fact head coach Sean McVay and the Los Angeles offensive staff is high on fellow running back Blake Corum, but he wound up with just 13 receptions on 19 targets the entire season; Williams had 44 catches on 59 targets.

Needless to say, I just don't see Corum as a threat in the passing game, whereas his success will likely impact Williams' numbers carrying the ball.

As for the yardage prop, Williams hit or cleared the magic number of 15 yards in Los Angeles' last six games of the season. In four of those games, he wound up with 21 yards or more through the air., and in the first meeting between these clubs last season, Williams hauled in eight receptions for 66 yards and two TDs.

Bottom line: I believe Williams will be heavily involved in the Rams' passing game. He gives Stafford a trusted option coming out of the backfield when he gets pressured by the opposing defense, which gives me confidence we can connect on both wagers, perhaps even in the first half.

Russell: The buzz around Stribling from the preseason shortened his odds for Offensive Rookie of the Year, but there's still decent payout available for a player who might have an instant connection with Purdy.

Stribling has earned a starting spot in the 49ers' three-receiver sets, and with Mike Evans getting the attention from the Rams' best coverage options in the red zone, and Deebo Samuel on their radar from years of facing the Niners with him, Stribling could parlay a big camp into a good look for a score.

Russell: We're already in on Nacua to lead the NFL in receiving touchdowns, so we'll be occasionally worried about whether the Rams' quick tosses to him at the goal line will be ruled laterals, but that's not going to be an issue in game-to-game anytime touchdown betting. Of course, Nacua is also a deep threat against a relatively weak San Francisco secondary.

Russell: With Nacua out for their Week 7 trip to London to take on the Jaguars, the Rams had to adjust their offense to feature bigger, three-tight end sets, at the same time that Colby Parkinson was getting healthier, having missed two of the first six games.

After their subsequent bye week, Parkinson's usage shot up the rest of the season, frequently playing more than 70% of the snaps, and scoring eight touchdowns. Those TDs came in seven of 13 games — a rate of better than 50% of the time. Given 4-to-1 odds imply that Parkinson scores just 20% of the time, these odds don't reflect Stafford's affection for throwing to his 6-foot-7 red zone target.

You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor, Matt Russell , at THE WINDOW .

articles.title: Chicago has its next Michael Jordan in Caleb Williams ... at least that's the hope
articles.summary: If Williams is able to keep the reigning NFC North champion Bears on their current trajectory, immortality awaits.
articles.body:
It's the kind of photo that, years from now, might decorate a hundred Chicago sports bars: Cubs, Bulls and Bears , all coming together like some kind of Windy City Avengers . There's the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong in the midst of a likely MVP season; two on-the-rise Bulls in Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis; and in the middle of it all, the guy who carries the hopes and dreams of an entire city on his shoulders.

At the start of his third season, Caleb Williams stands on the doorstep of glory. He's already given Chicago Bears fans the kind of hope they haven't had in decades. And if he's able to keep the reigning NFC North champion Bears on their current trajectory, well — immortality awaits. Nobody loves a hometown hero quite like Chicago.

These are exciting days in Chicago, the kind of days when you know you're at the start of something special. Crow-Armstrong should soon steal his way to the first 40-40 season in Cubs history and, with it, the National League MVP. Both the Cubs and White Sox are currently in postseason position. The Bulls, particularly Wilson, have potential. The Blackhawks' Connor Bedard is one of the most exciting players in hockey. Heck, even the pope is a Chicago sports fan.

But with all due respect to the other franchises, the Bears control the conversation, and it's on Williams to run the Bears.

"The entire city of Chicago is behind Caleb Williams in a way that I've never seen us get behind a Bears quarterback," says Kevin Kaduk, author of the Bears By 7 newsletter. "It's just a different feeling of confidence when he goes out there and works with Ben Johnson. What's also cool is that he's out and about around town. … When he goes to Wrigley Field to watch (PCA), he sits in the stands, not a luxury box."

Granted, the bar for Williams when he arrived was on the floor. At this point in their Bears tenure, previous quarterbacks Justin Fields and Mitch Trubisky were already hopeless. Indeed, since the fabled '85 Bears won Super Bowl XX, Chicago has started an astounding 45 quarterbacks, virtually none of whom left any lasting impression. Don't believe me? See how many you can name in Bears By 7's quiz . (We'll spot you Jim McMahon and Jim Harbaugh.)

When Chicago selected Williams with the first pick in the 2024 draft thanks to the generosity of the Carolina Panthers — the Bears' Week 1 opponent, coincidentally enough — no analysts questioned Williams' innate talent. Most, though, rightly questioned the Bears' ability to unlock that talent for the good of the team.

That proved a valid fear; although Williams himself set multiple rookie records, the Bears as a whole finished the 2024 season at 5-12, costing Matt Eberflus his job. Chicago snagged Johnson from division rival Detroit , and the results were immediate: a six-win improvement, a division championship, the franchise's first playoff victory since 2010 … and that intoxicating, unfamiliar feeling of hope.

So what do Williams and Johnson do for an encore? Work on fine-tuning an already fast machine, to start.

Williams set the franchise's single-season passing record with 3,942 yards — yes, Chicago still has never had a 4,000-yard quarterback — and a 27-to-7 touchdown-to-interception ratio. But he did so by slinging hero balls; his completion percentage of 58.1 ranked 32nd in the league, ahead of only Minnesota 's J.J. McCarthy . A second season under the tutelage of Johnson ought to help Williams manage the little things — footwork, timing, communication — to go along with his TikTok-worthy highlights.

"Late in some of those (2025) games, we were making some heroic plays . . . but it wasn't necessary if we execute in the first quarter and second quarter," Bears quarterback coach J.T. Barrett told Chicago media earlier this offseason . "We might be up two touchdowns by the time we get to the fourth quarter. We can be efficient and take what the defense is giving. You don't necessarily have to put the cape on and make those crazy plays because you already were killing them in the first three quarters."

Off the field, Williams is saying and doing all the right things to endear himself to Chicago. He sang the city's praises during a sweaty appearance as he devoured blazing-hot wings on the YouTube series "Hot Ones." And he surely lowered some blood pressures around town when he framed his future contract negotiations in terms of his love for the city.

"I obviously want to be here forever," Williams said last week, via the Chicago Sun-Times . "That's a goal of mine: to be at one place until I'm done, until I decide that it's over for me and I want to go home and ride off into the sun. ... I'll be here."

Analysts expect Chicago to post another playoff-worthy year , potentially even another division title. However, the Bears will face the toughest schedule in the NFL in 2026 based on opponents' winning percentage in 2025. It will be on Williams to succeed against that daunting slate.

If he's able to lead Chicago back into the playoffs, Williams will get standing ovations at every Cubs or Bulls game he attends next year. And although we're getting ahead of ourselves … what if, one day, he's able to do even more than that?

"I don't think there's any doubt he'd be at the top of the pantheon with people like Michael Jordan, Walter Payton and Patrick Kane," Kaduk said. "We've been talking about the Super Bowl XX Bears for more than 40 years, and if he finally delivered another one, we'd be talking about him for at least another 40."

articles.title: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Pleads No Contest to 2 Misdemeanor Charges, Including Battery
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest Thursday to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest Thursday to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.

Jacobs must pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs for the battery charge. Under an agreement with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge can be dismissed in a year if he fulfills terms that include staying out of trouble, avoiding the victim in this case, submitting to supervision, completing counseling and paying restitution to the victim.

"I fully understand the seriousness of the situation, and I take full responsibility," Jacobs said during an appearance in a Brown County court.

Browns QB Deshaun Watson Pleads Not Guilty to Speeding (AP)

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after Hobart-Lawrence police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

According to a criminal complaint, the woman's statement was corroborated by surveillance footage from the camera system in the garage where the incident occurred.

Jacobs was charged in late August and the NFL subsequently placed him on the commissioner's exempt list, which prevents the three-time Pro Bowl running back from playing or practicing but allows him to keep receiving a paycheck. Players on the commissioner's exempt list may be allowed at team facilities for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other non-football activities.

NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said Thursday that the league is monitoring the case, which is being reviewed under the league personal conduct policy, and Jacobs remains on the exempt list. The Packers had no immediate comment.

David Chesnoff, one of the lawyers representing Jacobs, said the running back already has begun counseling.

"This plea reflects Josh's acknowledgement of his actions and his acceptance of responsibility for these actions," Chesnoff said. "There are significant consequences for Josh, and he intends to meet all the requirements the court imposes under these negotiations."

According to the criminal complaint, Jacobs' girlfriend told police she had been looking through Jacobs' phone and saw he was talking to other women, and that she threw his phone in anger without breaking it. She told police that Jacobs had her phone and she told him he could look through it.

Police said the woman indicated she tried to retrieve her phone from Jacobs, but he grabbed her arm. They left the home in separate vehicles but eventually returned, and the woman later grabbed a second phone from a duffle bag. That led to the events in which she was trying to exit a garage door.

Jacobs entered his plea three days before the Packers open the season at Minnesota.

He is coming off a 2025 season during which he rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns. That followed a 2024 season in which he ran for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns while earning his third Pro Bowl selection.

Green Bay has no other running backs who rushed for more than 106 yards last season.

The only other running backs currently on Green Bay's 53-man roster are MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson. The Packers acquired Johnson from Pittsburgh the day that Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list.

Lloyd is a 2024 third-round pick who has played just one game over the last two seasons due to a variety of injuries, but he is healthy now. Lloyd said Jacobs has offered him advice about this upcoming game by telling him to "just stay where your feet are" and to "just be yourself."

articles.title: Seahawks news: Sam Darnold's MRI confirms he 'dodged bullet' with hip injury
articles.summary: On Wednesday evening, the Seattle Seahawks kicked off their 2026 NFL season with a thrilling home win over the New England Patriots in a rematch of last year...
articles.body:
On Wednesday evening, the Seattle Seahawks kicked off their 2026 NFL season with a thrilling home win over the New England Patriots in a rematch of last year's Super Bowl, which Seattle also won. The first half of this game was overshadowed by a hip injury to quarterback Sam Darnold , which thrust Drew Lock into the quarterback position for the rest of the evening.

However, thankfully, the team got a positive update on Darnold's status on Thursday.

"Seahawks QB Sam Darnold underwent an MRI on his hip this morning that team doctors still are reviewing to determine how much time he will miss. It is expected to be some, but for now the team believes it, as one source described, 'dodged a bullet,'" reported ESPN insider Adam Schefter on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Although more missed time isn't ideal, it's certainly good news that there doesn't seem to be any structural damage with Darnold's hip that could keep him out for a significant chunk of time.

Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network later reported on X that " Sam Darnold is expected to miss next week's game, but he should be back sooner, rather than later, sources say. Could be just a few weeks."

Also helping matters is the fact that the Seahawks are entering a light portion of their schedule over the coming couple of weeks, with the Arizona Cardinals and the Washington Commanders being their next two opponents.

Lock had a choppy start to the game but ended up making some big plays down the stretch, proving why the Seahawks trust him as their backup quarterback for situations like this.

Seattle now has a long week before they next hit the field on September 20 on the road vs the Cardinals.

articles.title: Former Browns, Pats lineman, College Hall of Famer dies
articles.summary: Bob McKay, the towering offensive tackle who helped define the University of Texas’ “Wishbone” offense and later spent nine seasons in the NFL, died Thursday...
articles.body:
Bob McKay, the towering offensive tackle who helped define the University of Texas' "Wishbone" offense and later spent nine seasons in the NFL , died Thursday. He was 78.

McKay was a first-team All-American, a national champion and a College Football Hall of Fame inductee whose career began in the small West Texas town of Crane. He was inducted into the T exas High School Football Hall of Fame in 2012 for his accomplishments at Crane High School, where he starred at end for the Golden Cranes and earned second-team all-state honors.

Darrell Royal's Texas program recruited McKay to Austin in 1966. He eventually developed into a 6-foot-5, 260-pound offensive tackle and became one of the most important players on the Longhorns' dominant teams of the late 1960s.

"He was a great leader," former Texas halfback Ted Koy said in a 2017 interview. "But even as big as he was, he didn't try to intimidate anybody. He led by cooperation. He had a way of convincing us to do it together. As a running back, you knew he was always going to do his job. If you just followed him, you were going in the right direction."

McKay played his final two college seasons in 1968 and 1969, helping Texas go 20-1-1, win two Southwest Conference championships and claim two Cotton Bowl victories.

In 1969, Texas went 11-0, won the national championship and finished the season with a 21-17 victory over Notre Dame in the Cotton Bowl. McKay was a consensus first-team All-American and All-Southwest Conference selection.

McKay entered the NFL as the 21st overall selection in the 1970 draft, taken by the Cleveland Browns . He played six seasons in Cleveland before joining the New England Patriots for three more seasons, finishing his professional career after the 1978 season. He appeared in 105 regular season NFL games, starting 71.

Both the Browns and Patriots reached the playoffs during McKay's tenure; he started playoff games in 1971, 1972 and 1976.

articles.title: MC&J: Ohio State hits the road for a clash with Texas in college football’s Week 2 slate
articles.summary: Score predictions for Ohio State-Texas, Oklahoma-Michigan and a bunch of other Week 2 games
articles.body:
Last week ATS: 16-9 (4-3 National, 12-6 B1G)

Last week was about as good of a start to the season as we could have asked for.

About the only things that are sticking with me is trusting Rutgers as a 30-point favorite over UMass last Thursday, along with seeing Ohio State cover late. Had the Buckeyes not scored that final touchdown, I would have been on the mark when it comes to my Buckeye score prediction.

Now to hope this week brings us similar success.

At least now we have a little bit to go on after seeing each team at least once. While I'm not going to say things are going to get easier going forward, at least it wouldn't be quite as much of a guessing game as it usually is in the first week.

Arizona State v. No. 10 Texas A&M (-14.5) – Saturday 9/12 12:00 p.m. ET – ABC

Both the Sun Devils and Aggies played cupcakes in their season openers, beating Morgan State and Missouri State by a combined score of 120-7. Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley was outstanding in his first start at quarterback for Arizona State, tossing six touchdowns.

The Sun Devils had three receivers go for over 100 yards in the blowout, but the difficult level will obviously be turned up on Saturday when they head to Kyle Field.

Texas A&M had a tough time getting things going in the first half, only leading Missouri State 19-0 before looking better in the second half. Back for another season in College Station are quarterback Marcel Reed, running back Rueben Owens II, and receiver Mario Craver. The offense also brought in Alabama transfer Isaiah Horton, who went for 76 yards and a score on his four catches.

Even though Texas A&M has designs on returning to the College Football Playoff for a second straight season, I think they get pushed by the Sun Devils. While I don't see Arizona State springing the upset on the road, I do think they keep the final score within two touchdowns.

No. 12 Alabama (-10.5) v. Kentucky – Saturday 9/12 3:30 p.m. ET – ABC

A 48-10 win over East Carolina doesn't fix everything in Tuscaloosa. New starting quarterback Keelon Russell impressed in his debut, totaling 340 yards against the Pirates. What is concerning about the Crimson Tide is the inconsistency of wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams.

Following a solid freshman season, Coleman-Williams regressed last year, and to start this year he ditched the gloves and dropped a couple passes. It'll be tough to trust Coleman-Williams throughout the season because obviously the drops are in his head.

Kentucky had little trouble with Youngstown State in Will Stein's first game as head coach, beating the Penguins 45-13 in Lexington. Notre Dame transfer quarterback Kenny Minchey threw four touchdowns in the victory, cementing himself as starting quarterback of the Wildcats.

Kentucky has made life difficult for a lot of SEC foes who have traveled to Lexington over the last few years and it's likely they do the same to Alabama on Saturday.

Arizona v. No. 15 BYU (-7.5) – Saturday 9/12 3:30 p.m. ET – FOX

Arizona has the look of being a difficult out in the Big 12 this year. The Wildcats have an experienced starting quarterback in Noah Fifita, who threw for 279 yards and two scores in a 35-7 win over Northern Arizona.

The Lumberjacks could get nothing going on the ground against Arizona, totaling -7 yards rushing. BYU could be in a lot of trouble if the Wildcats can replicate the five sacks they recorded in their season opener.

Unfortunately for Arizona, BYU has quarterback Bear Bachmeier and running back L.J. Martin returning in the backfield from a team who only lost two games last season, both to Texas Tech. As if the Cougars weren't scary enough on offense, true freshman Legend Glasker caught three touchdowns in his BYU debut last week.

Despite Arizona having the talent to keep pace with the Cougars, the home-field advantage in Provo will allow BYU to win by more than a touchdown.

No. 11 Oklahoma (-5.5) v. Michigan – Saturday 9/12 12:00 p.m. ET – FOX

Michigan's first game under Kyle Whittingham was an all-around embarrassment. The Wolverines should have lost to Western Michigan but were gifted an extra second and then somehow Bryce Underwood hit a hail mary to beat the Broncos.

As if winning in that fashion wasn't embarrassing enough, then fans stormed the field. Imagine Ohio State fans doing the same after barely squeaking by a team like Bowling Green.

A huge reason why Michigan struggled on Saturday night was because of the play of Bryce Underwood. The quarterback was just 12-22 for 170 yards, a touchdown, and a interception. That isn't the type of performance from someone getting as big of a bag as Underwood is. The Wolverines also couldn't get much going on the ground, rushing for just 106 yards.

Unlike Michigan, Oklahoma handled their business in their opener against UTEP, defeating the Miners 51-0. John Mateer picked up where he left off last season, throwing for 225 yards and three scores. The Sooners also forced two turnovers and returned a punt for a touchdown.

Michigan will likely look better than they did last week, but they aren't at the level of Oklahoma.

Iowa State v. No. 21 Iowa (-13.5) – Saturday 9/12 7:30 p.m. ET – NBC

This year's edition of El Assico will have a different look, as Iowa State has turned to Jimmy Rogers after Matt Campbell left Ames to take the Penn State job. Rogers has a tough task this season since less than 50 percent of the team's production from last year's team is back.

Arkansas State transfer Jaylen Raynor started for the Cyclones last week, but completed just 50 percent of his passes.

Iowa has a new quarterback. Hank Brown was 12-20 for 129 yards and a touchdown. Not exactly massive numbers but they look a lot better when considering the Hawkeyes ran for 289 yards in the 40-0 win over Northern Illinois. We have become accustomed to Iowa finding success despite inconsistent quarterback play since they are usually strong on defense and special teams.

Nearly two touchdowns might seem like a lot to lay in this one but not only are the Hawkeyes at home, they are definitely the more complete team entering this game. Iowa takes care of their in-state rivals under the lights at Kinnick.

No. 1 Ohio State v. No. 4 Texas (-1.5) – Saturday 9/12 7:30 p.m. ET – ABC

Over the last two seasons Ohio State has won both meetings with the Longhorns, beating Texas in the Cotton Bowl in January 2025, followed by a 14-7 win in Columbus in last season's opener. Now Ohio State will try and complete the trifecta by beating the Longhorns three straight times at three different venues.

The Buckeyes looked great in their season opener against Ball State. Unlike last season when a lot was unknown about Arch Manning heading into the Ohio State game after he took over as full-time starter at quarterback, Manning completed 74 percent of his passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns against Texas State.

Manning has plenty of weapons to work with in NC State transfer running back Hollywood Smothers, along with receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman . Then there is defensive star Colin Simmons, who likely has learned his lesson when it comes to making bulletin board statements prior to the clash with the Buckeyes.

In the end it is going to come down to coaching. Ryan Day just has Steve Sarkisian's number. Even though Ohio State will be heading to Austin on Saturday night, it's not like the Buckeyes aren't familiar with taking on the Longhorns in tough environments since they already played the Texas in Dallas less than two years ago.

This has the makings of another tight game, but Ohio State finds a way to make it a hat trick against the Longhorns.

articles.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs pleads no contest to charges of battery, criminal damage to property
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested in May and has since been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the NFL.
articles.body:
Content warning: The following article contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs entered a plea of no contest on Thursday to charges of battery and criminal damage to property.

Jacobs was arrested in May and was originally booked on five charges.

According to ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Jacobs' no contest plea was accepted by the Brown County Court in Wisconsin on the conditions that he is not involved in future criminal acts, avoids contact with the victim, undergoes counseling, remains under supervision and pays restitution to the victim.

Jacobs was also ordered to pay a $1,000 fine on the misdemeanor battery charge.

"I fully understand the seriousness of the situation and take full responsibility," Jacobs told the court.

According to a statement from Jacobs' attorney, the court is suspending the criminal damage to property count for 12 months. It will then be dismissed as part of the agreement.

"With this agreement, Josh has accepted responsibility for his conduct and resolved this matter," the statement read. "Today's resolution is set against a career-long history of Josh's community work while in the NFL, which has centered on the circumstances of his early life."

The hearing was originally scheduled for Nov. 17 before being moved to Thursday, three days before the Packers open the season against the Minnesota Vikings .

The alleged incident occurred on May 23 at Jacobs' home. The criminal complaint, according to ESPN , stated that a woman was trying to leave Jacobs' garage when he "grabbed her and threw her to the ground, and she struck her head, suffering an injury."

The Brown County district attorney in Wisconsin said the surveillance video from Jacobs' garage corroborates the alleged victim's claims of what transpired, per The Athletic .

On Aug. 30, Jacobs was placed on the NFL's Commissioner's Exempt List , barring him from practicing or playing for the Packers until he is removed. The league said on Thursday there is "no timetable" for when any punishment could be handed down.

"We have been closely monitoring all developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy. There is no change to his status as he remains on the Commissioner's Exempt list."

Per the NFL's collective bargaining agreement, the standard suspension for domestic violence is six games.

Jacobs had 929 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns last season, his second with the Packers after starting his career with the Las Vegas Raiders . He signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers in free agency ahead of the 2024 campaign.

articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa Goes to Ground with Oblique Injury in Video from Falcons Practice Ahead of Week 1
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa was officially limited at Thursday's practice after suffering an oblique injury.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa was officially limited at Thursday's practice after suffering an oblique injury.

Based on multiple reports and a video shared by Reggie Chatman Jr. from Atlanta's 11Alive, Tagovailoa was in visible distress at one point and briefly went to the ground:

Tagovailoa had some minor back trouble early in training camp, though he suited up for two of Atlanta's three preseason games.

The 2023 Pro Bowler was set to start Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Falcons' quarterback battle became a foregone conclusion with Michael Penix Jr. still working his way back from a torn ACL.

For now, Cooper Rush is backing up Tagovailoa, with Jack Strand third on the unofficial depth chart . Rush told reporters he took all of the first-team reps in practice on Thursday.

In the event Tua is ruled out, some fans will likely call for Strand to vault into the starting role.

Rush is a career backup who combined to go 25-of-39 for 251 yards and four interceptions his two starts with the Baltimore Ravens in 2025.

Strand is an undrafted rookie who competed at Minnesota State Moorhead, a Division II school. Needless to say, the NFL would be a massive step up, but a team in Atlanta's position may not have much to lose.

The Falcons are already treading water for a year at quarterback by leaning on Tagovailoa and Penix. Why not see if they hit the lottery with Strand?

Of course, this is all a moot point if Tagovailoa only had a minor scare Thursday and is deemed good to go in Week 1.

articles.title: Sean McVay's Trade Value Addressed by Rams GM After Being Asked How Many Picks HC is Worth
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams general manager Les Snead has no interest in trading head coach Sean McVay.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams general manager Les Snead has no interest in trading head coach Sean McVay.

"If I could write on this whiteboard here, I would write, 'There's no trade for Sean McVay,'" he said during an interview with 60 Minutes .

When pressed if he would give up his head coach for three first-round picks, he said he wouldn't even "pull the trigger" for four or five.

While it is typically players and draft picks included in trades in the NFL, there is some precedent for a coach trade. The Denver Broncos traded a first- and second-round draft pick to the New Orleans Saints for head coach Sean Payton and a third-round pick in 2023.

At the time, Payton had stepped away from coaching but still had two years remaining on his contract with the Saints and wanted to return to the NFL sidelines.

Given that as a baseline, trading McVay for four or five first-round picks might be an ideal investment for the Rams. However, Snead made it clear it's not something he would even consider.

Perhaps that shouldn't be so surprising given McVay's track record.

In nine years as the head coach in Los Angeles, the NFC West team has been to the Super Bowl twice, won a Lombardi Trophy and been to the playoffs seven times. The Rams have more NFC Championship Game appearances (three) than seasons missing the playoffs (two) under McVay's leadership.

They are once again positioned to challenge for a Lombardi Trophy this season with a star-studded roster that includes Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Aaron Donald, among others.

And they will have a coach worth more than a handful of first-round draft picks in the general manager's eyes leading the way.

Ahead of his first official game back with the New York Giants, Odell Beckham Jr. is also returning to a look from his past.

Beckham went back to his old blond hairstyle before declaring: "You know what time it is."

Beckham previously explained to GQ in 2016 that he originally went blond leading up to the NFL scouting combine in 2014 and "it just got blonder and blonder."

There have been times when Beckham brought it back as a bit of a superstitious ritual to help him and his team succeed. He had his blond locks in 2020 with the Cleveland Browns.

Beckham earned a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster coming out of the preseason, seven years after he was originally traded by New York to Cleveland. He will make his first appearance back with the Giants on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Updated Injury Status and Fantasy Outlook for Raiders vs. Dolphins in NFL Week 1
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, who suffered a sprained ankle during an Aug. 23 practice, said he'll play in his team's season-opening matchup on Sunday vs. the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, who suffered a sprained ankle during an Aug. 23 practice , said he'll play in his team's season-opening matchup on Sunday vs. the Miami Dolphins.

That should extinguish any remaining doubt about his status, on top of the fact that Jeanty was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, per the Raiders' injury report .

With all that being said, the expectation here is for Jeanty to handle his usual full workload for the first game in head coach Klint Kubiak's tenure.

Jeanty, the 2024 Heisman Trophy runner-up, was selected sixth overall in the NFL draft after a stellar career at Boise State.

Last year, Jeanty amassed 975 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 266 carries (3.7 yards per attempt). He also caught 55 passes for 346 yards and five more scores.

Jeanty didn't have the most efficient year in a bad season for the Raiders offense overall (last in scoring). Still, there is hope in Kubiak, the former Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator who helped lead his old team to a Super Bowl title last February. Kubiak is a bright offensive mind who can unlock Jeanty's potential, leading to a more efficient, productive Year 2.

Per the Fantasy Pros point-per-reception draft rankings, which were the result of a consensus of 177 fantasy football experts, Jeanty ranked 11th among running backs and 28th overall entering this season.

There's no doubt Jeanty is an every-week starting running back in season-long leagues. He was 11th last year among running backs in PPR points (245.1) and 30th overall despite averaging just 3.7 yards per carry.

The big question is whether Jeanty could cede some touches to rookie Mike Washington Jr., who has shined in the preseason and has earned time. As ESPN's Ryan McFadden noted, Kubiak talked about Jeanty as a bellcow, but that may not be the case given Washington's emergence.

Still, Jeanty is the clear No. 1, and he seems past the ankle injury. Fantasy players should start Jeanty with confidence, and finishing comfortably as a top-five running back in points per game this year isn't out of the question.

articles.title: Browns QB Deshaun Watson Pleads Not Guilty to Speeding
articles.summary: CLEVELAND (AP) — Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has pleaded not guilty after receiving a speeding ticket on Aug. 26.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has pleaded not guilty after receiving a speeding ticket on Aug. 26.

Watson entered the plea Wednesday in Cleveland Municipal Court, according to court records. The next hearing is set for Sept. 23.

Watson, who turns 31 on Monday, was pulled over by Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers for allegedly going 86 mph in a 60 mph zone in a 2022 Ram pickup truck on Interstate 480 in Cleveland during morning rush hour.

Watson will make his first start since Week 7 of the 2024 season when the Browns open the season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. He won the starting quarterback competition over Shedeur Sanders.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield Reacts to Bucs Contract Extension, 'Caught Me Off Guard' After Offseason Talks
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield says he was surprised by contract offers including the three-year, $165 million extension he signed earlier this week despite cutting off his involvement in negotiations at the start of training camp.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield says he was surprised by contract offers including the three-year, $165 million extension he signed earlier this week despite cutting off his involvement in negotiations at the start of training camp.

Mayfield told ESPN's Peter Schrager he hadn't known his agent and the Buccaneers were still in negotiations until he and his wife Emily received a call Monday night.

"I started training camp. I told my agent, 'Listen, I'm done talking about it. I'm done pacing the house thinking about it, unless there's something that you guys talk about and it's worth bringing to my attention,'" Mayfield told Schrager in an appearance on ESPN's Big Day.

Mayfield continued, "He contacted Emily and I on Monday night, about 6 p.m. I guess they had been talking since later in the week, last week, which was news to me, so caught me off guard as well. He presented a couple options, and went from there."

Mayfield previously told reporters he had agreed to the final terms of the contract while watching a theatrical re-release of the movie Cars with teammates and their families.

The Buccaneers announced around 6 p.m. Tuesday Mayfield had been signed to the largest contract in franchise history.

The deal will put Mayfield on the same tier as top quarterbacks like Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence and Matthew Stafford by matching their $55 million in annual average salary.

The contract also included $110 million in new guarantees to go alongside the $40 million in guaranteed money Mayfield was already set to earn this season, per ESPN's Dan Graziano .

Mayfield will look to start his first game since signing the historic deal strong when the Buccaneers open the 2026 season on the road this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa limited in practice after injuring oblique just days before Week 1 start
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa needed to sit on the grass after sustaining the injury.
articles.body:
After waiting the entire preseason, the Atlanta Falcons finally named Tua Tagovailoa as the team's starting quarterback in Week 1. A few days later, and that status could be in jeopardy.

Tagovailoa sustained an oblique injury during practice Thursday. After touching his back and sitting on the ground, Tagovailoa did not throw again in the portion of practice attended by the media.

Footage of the injury shows Tagovailoa gingerly taking a few steps away from the action before sitting in the grass. He was able to get up shortly after and jogged down the field.

Since Tagovailoa appeared to grab his back at first, many thought he re-aggravated a back injury he dealt with back in July. That injury caused Tagovailoa to miss time early in training camp . But it sounds as though Thursday was a new issue for the quarterback.

Falcons backup Cooper Rush filled in for Tagovailoa after the injury. After practice, Rush said he took every rep with the starters Thursday.

Before Thursday, Tagovailoa's grasp on a starting spot was in question. Michael Penix Jr. reportedly pushed Tagovailoa for that role, but Penix still needs more time to recover after tearing his ACL last season.

Once Penix is healthy — and he was listed as a full participant in practice Thursday — it's unclear whether the Falcons will still stick with Tagovailoa. Prior to the injury scare Thursday, a report emerged suggesting the Falcons would release Tagovailoa if/when he loses his starting role . That doesn't paint the rosiest picture just days before Tagovailoa is set to make his first start.

Tagovailoa's fall from grace in the NFL has come quickly . After leading the NFL in passing yards in 2023, injuries have limited Tagovailoa's upside in recent seasons. He sustained yet another concussion early in 2024, prompting concern for his future in the NFL. Tagovailoa was able to return and play after the concussion and still managed to post solid numbers.

But things regressed in 2025. Tagovailoa threw 20 touchdowns against 15 interceptions in 14 games before he was benched. Once the season was over, the Dolphins decided to cut Tagovailoa, who carried a massive dead-cap hit.

That paved the way for Tagovailoa to sign with the Falcons in the offseason. While he ultimately won the starting job, things haven't gone well for the veteran in his short time with his new franchise.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Says Tom Brady Has Been 'Unbelievable' Resource for Raiders QBs Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins says minority team owner Tom Brady has been "very available" as a resource for the Las Vegas Raiders' quarterbacks in the lead-up to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins says minority team owner Tom Brady has been "very available" as a resource for the Las Vegas Raiders' quarterbacks in the lead-up to the 2026 season.

Cousins told reporters Wednesday he has regularly reached out to Brady this offseason while leading a quarterback room staffed by rookie backup Fernando Mendoza and third-stringer Aidan O'Connell.

"I've really enjoyed having him as a resource," Cousins said (h/t Vegas Sports Today's Sean Zittel). "I mean, when I first got here, I was like, 'Wait, so I can just text him, and he'll give me 23 years of pro football experience, he'll text me back?' They're like, 'Yeah.'"

Cousins continued, "You can sit in a meeting with Fernando and Aidan and say, 'Why don't we just ask Tom what he would do?'

"Sometimes, you're like, is he going to get back to us in a day or two? And many times, it's two minutes, and we've got a response. So that's been a joy to have a resource."

Mendoza previously mentioned Brady's involvement in the Raiders quarterback room during an interview with Front Office Sports' David Rumsey earlier this summer.

"We had a question about a specific concept, and we were all there," Mendoza told Rumsey in June. "Kirk was able to voice memo Tom really quick, and he got back to us, and it was a great answer that we took a lot from."

General manager John Spytek said in February he expected Brady to be involved with the Raiders' decision-making both in free agency and the draft, through which the franchise brought in Cousins and Mendoza, respectively.

Schrager indicated last week on the Pat McAfee Show Brady could also have had a role in the decision to name Cousins starter over Mendoza.

"As long as Tom Brady was a part of this, and I'm told this year he has been very vocal and has been a part of it, they weren't going to rush their first overall pick," Schrager said.

Cousins will now help that guidance from Brady this offseason will pay off with a Week 1 win against the Miami Dolphins when the season officially kicks off Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Says He Just Found Out Bengals' Start Time for Week 1 vs. Bucs in Funny Video
articles.summary: It's safe to say Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase hasn't been studying the schedule to this point.
articles.body:
It's safe to say Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase hasn't been studying the schedule to this point.

He told reporters Thursday he found out "today" that the team's opening game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

"I'm finding out the game is at 1 o'clock, I do not like that," he said. "To be honest, I do not like playing in 1 o'clock games. So that means I have to wake up a little earlier than usual."

While one way to spin his comment would be to say Chase enjoys playing under the primetime spotlight, he did highlight that he will have to wake up earlier for an early afternoon game.

He might not want to check the schedule in the immediate aftermath of his comments either, as the Bengals are slated to play at 1 p.m. ET in each of their first seven games of the 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson Talks Ja'Marr Chase 'Love-Hate Relationship' and Competition to Be NFL's No. 1 WR
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson detailed his friendly rivalry with Cincinnati Bengals star receiver and former LSU teammate Ja'Marr Chase.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson detailed his friendly rivalry with Cincinnati Bengals star receiver and former LSU teammate Ja'Marr Chase.

"It's definitely a love-hate relationship, but it has to be," Jefferson said in an interview for Boardroom with Taylor Rooks (34:24 mark). "Just because of how competitive we are and how much this sport really means to us. We don't ever like to be number two. No one ever likes to be number two. But to have two guys that's on a similar level, superstars of a league that has all of the talent in the world, that's able to take a franchise to the next level, for us to be on that same team at LSU is pretty crazy to actually think about."

"That transformed into us always competing against each other. He's on one side, I'm on the other side. We're always competing for who's gonna get the most touchdowns, who's gonna get the most yards. Having that friendly battle but also understanding how far to take it. We're not overly stepping on boundaries, we're not overly disrespecting one another, we're not overly calling each other out. We respect one another's game, but we both think we're number one."

Before their NFL careers, Jefferson and Chase spent two seasons together at LSU from 2018-19.

During their final year as teammates, they combined for 3,320 receiving yards and 38 touchdowns while playing key roles in a Tigers offense that helped the team compile a perfect 15-0 record and capture a national championship.

Jefferson and Chase have remained dominant upon entering the NFL as first-round picks in 2020 and 2021, respectively.

Jefferson has racked up 8,480 receiving yards and 42 touchdown catches in six seasons, while Chase has amassed 6,837 receiving yards and 54 touchdowns in five years.

Jefferson has tallied four Pro Bowl nods, two First Team All-Pro selections and an Offensive Player of the Year award.

As for Chase, he's received five Pro Bowl selections, two First Team All-Pro honors and an Offensive Rookie of the Year award.

While both players are prepared to battle for the title of the NFL's top wide receiver during the 2026 season, there doesn't appear to be any animosity between the two.

articles.title: Everything Malik Nabers Said About His Week 1 Status for Giants vs. Cowboys, Pitch Count, More
articles.summary: Malik Nabers says he's still not certain if he'll be on the field when the New York Giants open the season Sunday against the visiting Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers says he's still not certain if he'll be on the field when the New York Giants open the season Sunday against the visiting Dallas Cowboys.

"I'll let God tell me," Nabers said Thursday about when he'll know about his Week 1 availability (h/t SNY ). "Keeping my faith, and He'll let me know, and I'll know when it's time."

Nabers has been recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season.

He said Thursday he expects the Giants to let him decide both whether he plays and if he's on a snap count this weekend.

"I wouldn't want anyone to tell me I'm going to be on the pitch count, because at the end of the day, it's my career and it's my body," Nabers said. "If a pitch count is in the conversation, then I would lead that conversation. That decision would be on me."

The Giants are preparing to open the season at MetLife Stadium this Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: The Rams built a super team. Seattle showed why they own Super Bowl
articles.summary: The Super Bowl champ Seahawks showed why they might be just the team to upend the Rams' super team (again).
articles.body:
SEATTLE – Ernest Jones IV's face was bruised and battered, blood creeping from a bandage applied to the outside edge of his puffy left eye. He certainly had the look of a prize fighter who had emerged victorious after going the distance.

"It's a 12-round fight, man, that's all it is," Jones, a linebacker and team captain, said in the Lumen Field locker room Wednesday night after the Seattle Seahawks got off the mat to mount a late charge to a 13-10 victory over the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl 60 rematch that kicked off the NFL 's 2026 season.

Top moments from Patriots vs. Seahawks in the NFL season opener

The Seahawks may be the league's reigning heavyweight and perhaps the football version of Rocky – tough, relentless and full of heart, if not exactly a champion out of central casting ... and maybe a touch disrespected as a result . Then their quarterback, Sam Darnold, was lost to a hip injury after the season's first drive, and an offense already under the leadership of rookie coordinator Brian Fleury needed more than a half before it stopped wobbling. Budding star safety Nick Emmanwori sat out amid his ongoing recovery from ankle surgery in July.

But it wasn't enough adversity to end a winning streak that now stands at 11 games.

"Really remarkable. So proud to get the win," Seattle coach Mike Macdonald said.

"We talk about the '26 Seahawks and understanding our identity and who we are – that definitely revealed the type of team we have. We have a resilient, tough bunch that sticks together. I am really proud of the effort. Just really proud to be a Seahawk today."

But while New England is certainly a worthy challenger for the belt, losing a split decision in a non-title bout Wednesday after getting knocked out by the Seahawks in the Super Bowl, the Patriots are not Ivan Drago.

Drago, aka the Los Angeles Rams – the foreboding, seemingly invincible machine coming for Rocky's crown – fight the formidable San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night in Australia. The Rams , who were perhaps one play away from supplanting Seattle as the NFC's Super Bowl entry earlier this year, are notably new and improved following the offseason trade for two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett (talk about an imposing monster from central casting), the return of three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald (talk about an imposing monster from central casting) and acquisitions of former Kansas City Chiefs cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . Adding a quartet of that caliber to a loaded roster that already had ample glitz and glam, and the Rams look the part of a prohibitive favorite.

Meanwhile, Rocky – meaning the Seahawks – know they're being counted out in plenty of quarters because the tale of the tape doesn't favor them.

"They're easily motivated, because there's a lot of noise out there about how great the L.A. Rams are, and that's low-hanging fruit for Coach Macdonald as he motivates and gets this group rightly focused to answer," longtime Pittsburgh Steelers coach and new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin said prior to Wednesday night's kickoff.

And so are intangibles, even if they can't be quantified.

Darnold may never be a league MVP like Rams QB Matthew Stafford , but he is beloved in a close-knit Seattle locker room. The admiration for and trust in backup quarterback Drew Lock , who led the Seahawks to the final 13 points of Wednesday night's win, was nearly as evident following the win.

Macdonald has fostered a winning culture focused on "chasing edges," relentlessly seeking small advantages that can lead to massive results in crucial situations. And while he may not have players the caliber of Stafford, Garrett, Donald, McDuffie and Puka Nacua , Seattle also showed it's not relying on a top-heavy roster but one imbued with depth and hungry, less-established players throughout

Who are Josh Jobe and Nehemiah Pritchett ? Unsung Seattle corners who both picked off New England's Drake Maye , the runner-up to Stafford for league MVP in 2025, Wednesday – Jobe pilfering Maye's final pass into the end zone to secure the victory. Who is Jadarian Price? A rookie running back charged with replacing departed Super Bowl 60 MVP Kenneth Walker III . Price showed glimpses of the slashing game-breaker he could soon be as a pro, and there was a feeling from Macdonald and others that he's already earned more touches moving forward than the 12 he got in his pro debut.

"We practice like hell. Those guys are going to get their reps," Jones said.

"And we trust guys like Drew, we trust guys in the secondary who are coming up. It's a trust thing, and it's something we've built through care.

And now the Seahawks have the first win of the season in hand and 11 days to recuperate before their next game (against the lowly Arizona Cardinals ) while the Rams sandwich 30 hours worth of trans-Pacific flight time around what should be a stern test from the Niners.

The Seahawks have passed their first exam, armed with the knowledge more studying will be required to beat the Rams, whom they don't face for the first time until Christmas.

"It was the perfect type of game that you'd want for Week 1. Lot of adversity. Wasn't very clean. But we stuck together," said safety Julian Love , who had Seattle's third pick off Maye.

"That's probably the number one thing that we have is we're just going to find a way. It might be scoring a bunch of points, it might be shutting out a team, special teams making plays, whatever. We'll find a way. I think that's a sign of a great team is just to be able to do it multiple ways."

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Points Finger at Patriots QB Drake Maye Over Late-Game Decision-Making in Opener Loss
articles.summary: It takes big blunders to let go of a 10-0 lead in the final quarter and that’s what had happened in the Week 1 game between the New England Patriots and the...
articles.body:
It takes big blunders to let go of a 10-0 lead in the final quarter and that's what had happened in the Week 1 game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks . Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions that ultimately allowed the Seahawks to close the gap and mount a comeback in the fourth quarter.

Such kinds of defeats are always harder to swallow, and Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel didn't hold back pointing to his quarterback partly responsible for it.

Mike Vrabel calls out Drake Maye's 'three interceptions'

The New England Patriots controlled the game for three quarters against the Seattle Seahawks , holding a 10-0 lead heading into the final period. Then the offense completely unraveled. Quarterback Drake Maye threw interceptions on each of the team's final three possessions, handing Seattle the momentum and the 13-10 victory.

Maye's first pick came on a deep shot that Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett intercepted. Seattle immediately capitalized, with receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba scoring a 45-yard touchdown that tied the game at 10-10. The second interception occurred on third-and-14. Maye's pass intended for DeMario Douglas was tipped at the line and landed in the hands of safety Julian Love . Seahawks followed with a 26-yard Jason Myers field goal that put the Seahawks ahead for good.

The decisive third pick sealed the outcome. With 26 seconds left, Maye was flushed to his right and forced a throw toward wide receiver Mack Hollins in the end zone. Cornerback Josh Jobe read the play, undercut the route, and intercepted the pass in bounds. Had Maye simply thrown the ball away, kicker Andy Borregales would have had a roughly 34-yard field-goal attempt to tie the game.

Head coach Mike Vrabel refused to sugarcoat the result. Three interceptions on the final three drives directly caused the collapse from a 10-0 lead. He made it clear that Maye understands the standard.

"We want to be aggressive, not reckless. You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that," Mike Vrabel said .

Drake Maye also reflected on his performance, and he didn't take easy on himself. While talking about his performance, he described his performance as "unacceptable" and

Drake Maye vows to be better in the coming games

Maye was candid about his performance after the game, taking full responsibility for the loss.

"I thought we had the game under control," Maye said . "I thought we had a good plan to try to start chipping away and be patient. Lost patience and it cost us, decisions that cost us the game on my part, on my end. I vow to myself to be better and realize it's a long season. But at the same time, you can't have those. It's unacceptable."

The quarterback was particularly hard on himself over the crucial late turnover that sealed the Patriots' fate.

"I was trying to get rid of it… realized Mack [Hollins] was back there… and didn't put enough on it to get it out. And it was just unacceptable. We had a chance to send it to overtime at the worst. And the only thing you can do is turn the ball over. And that's what I did," he added.

He also acknowledged forcing earlier throws, including one down the sideline to Romeo Doubs that contributed to the first interception.

After their 13-10 season-opening loss to the Seattle Seahawks, the New England Patriots return home for Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, September 20, 2026. The Patriots will have 11 days to recover and prepare after the Wednesday night loss.

articles.title: NFL Reacts as Former Seahawk Dre’Mont Jones’ Early Sack Leaves Sam Darnold’s Status Unclear
articles.summary: Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks began their 2026 NFL campaign with a win against the New England Patriots. The two sides met in the NFL Kickoff Game, wh...
articles.body:
Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks began their 2026 NFL campaign with a win against the New England Patriots . The two sides met in the NFL Kickoff Game, which was a repeat of last season's Super Bowl game. The Seahawks emerged victorious once more, winning with a score of 13-10.

However, it was not all good news for the Seahawks. Darnold suffered a serious injury during the game which has shocked the NFL.

Sam Darnold suffers injury in first game of the season

Darnold suffered a right hip injury on just the fifth play of the 2026 NFL season during the team's season opener against the Patriots at Lumen Field. It happened on the third-and-6 during Seattle's opening possession. Darnold dropped back, could not find an open receiver, and attempted to extend the play before being sacked from behind by Patriots defensive lineman Dre'Mont Jones.

Jones drove Darnold to the turf , with the quarterback's right leg and hip absorbing the primary force of the impact as he landed awkwardly on his right knee. The quarterback rose and limped off the field under his own power. He initially waved off medical staff while pressing his right hand into his hip to loosen it but later entered the sideline medical tent for evaluation. He then limped to the locker room accompanied by team personnel.

The Seahawks first listed him as questionable with a hip injury before ruling him out prior to halftime. Darnold only managed to complete 1 of 2 passes for 13 yards before exiting. In his absence, backup Drew Lock entered the game.

It is currently unknown what is the true extent of the injury and what his recovery timeline will be. Head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed after the game that it was not a fracture, and that a CT scan at Harborview Medical Center produced encouraging but inconclusive results. Many fans were not happy to see Darnold get injured.

NFL fans react as Sam Darnold suffers injury

Many fans on social media expressed their disappointment for Darnold suffering an injury.

One user said , "I feel sorry for Sam Darnold man, Busting your butt all offseason only to get injured first series."

A second user wrote , "Hip injuries linger for QBs. Is this the end of Darnold's audition in Seattle?"

A third user replied , "Tough blow for the Seahawks. Hope Sam Darnold makes a quick recovery.

Another added , "This is going to kill the Seahawks, that defense has to stay healthy if this is a long term Injury in order for them to be considered Wild Card come playoff time."

A fifth user commented , "Really unfortunate for Darnold. From Seattle's side, this becomes a pretty big test of their depth and preparation."

It remains to be seen what the full extent of Sam Darnold's injury is and when he will be back for the Seahawks.
